author: G. G. Haynes
title: Detroit Fire Department announces death of Lieutenant Dale Fahoome after cancer battle
text:
Detroit | wikipedia.org
Detroit | wikipedia.org
The Detroit Fire Department has announced the death of Lieutenant Dale Fahoome, a veteran firefighter who served for 27 years. Lt. Fahoome died on Tuesday, January 27, 2026, after battling Stage 4 cancer. His passing is being treated as a presumed Line of Duty Death under Michigan’s Cancer Presumption legislation.
Lt. Fahoome was born and raised on Detroit’s east side and graduated from Cass Technical High School before joining the department in 1999. Throughout his career, he was recognized for his commitment to serving both his colleagues and the community.
He was also known for his work outside of firefighting, co-founding Motor City Fire, a nonprofit organization that supports firefighters and their families.
“Dale was the embodiment of service — brave in fire, generous in spirit, and relentless in his fight,” said Detroit Fire Chief David Nelson. “His loss is immeasurable, and his legacy will live on through every life he touched.”
Funeral and memorial arrangements are pending and will be announced once finalized with Lt. Fahoome’s family.
The department expressed condolences to Lt. Fahoome’s family, fellow firefighters, and all those affected by his passing.
